note: Pass with three disclosures. (1) SHIPPED WORDING IS ENGLISH; THE STUDY ADMINISTERED FRENCH. Participants were recruited 'via an advertisement on social networks in France' and 653 of 674 wave-0 respondents are coded Country=1 (France); the questionnaire was French. Neither the OSF deposit (which holds exactly two files - PsyR_lockdown2020.R and data.PsyR_lockdown2020.csv, confirmed against the OSF v2 file listing; the .R is an lme4/mediation analysis script containing no item strings) nor the Frontiers article and its supplements (Europe PMC reports hasSuppl=N) carries any French item wording. Per the 2026-09-01 fallback rule the CPC-12's own published English goes in the base fields, the _translated columns stay empty, language=French, text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=official_instrument_english (Lorenz et al.'s own English rendering of their German scale, S1 Appendix). No machine translation was produced. (2) MAPPING IS ORDER-INFERRED AND ONLY PARTLY VERIFIED. data/pellerin2020_covid_resources.py melts the literal column list ['Opt_1','Opt_2','Opt_3'] out of the OSF CSV, so the IRW item code IS the source column name (code-derivation pattern 1) - but that CSV is a plain header row with no variable or value labels, so it ties the code to nothing textual. The assignment Opt_1/Opt_2/Opt_3 -> CPC-12 items 4/5/6 is inferred from the CPC-12's own item order, hence mapping_basis=paper_order. Two content-derived predictions were tested against the deposit at wave 0 (n=674) and both hold: (P1) only item 4 references remaining lifespan ('the life ahead of me'), and Opt_1 correlates -0.185 with Age against -0.079 for Opt_2 and -0.038 for Opt_3 (Steiger z=-3.27, p=0.0011 and z=-3.74, p=0.0002), pinning Opt_1; (P2) items 4 and 5 share the AFF parent scale while item 6 is imported from the LOT-R, and r(Opt_1,Opt_2)=0.636 exceeds r(Opt_1,Opt_3)=0.473 (Steiger z=+7.29, p<1e-12). P2 is what separates Opt_2 from Opt_3, and it rests on an assumption about parent-scale cohesion rather than on any published per-item statistic - items 5 and 6 are near-synonymous expectancy statements and the age route does not distinguish them (z=-1.45, p=0.15). Recorded as PARTIAL, not VERIFIED. Subscale membership is separately exact: the deposit's own Optimism column equals rowMeans(Opt_1..Opt_3) to 3.6e-15, with M=4.89 SD=1.29 at wave 0 against the article's Table 1 M=4.84 SD=1.31 (the article's descriptives are computed on its analysed subsample after excluding the 21 respondents living outside France and one minor). See verify_pellerin2020_cpc_optimism.R. (3) RIGHTS: no block, one caution quoted. The CPC-12 was built specifically as an open alternative to the licensed PCQ and is published in full in a CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE appendix by its own authors; nothing reserves a fee, permission, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution right, so silence is permission (irw#1945 test). Item 6 ('Overall, I expect more good things to happen to me than bad') is LOT-R item 10, and the LOT-R carries a ship_with_note verdict in itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv on the strength of its author's caution: 'Please note that this is a research instrument, not intended for clinical applications' (https://www.psy.miami.edu/faculty/ccarver/lot-r.html). That clause disclaims fitness rather than reserving a right, so it does not block; the register verdict is applied, not re-derived. (4) TRANSCRIPTION AND SHAPE. item_text is the S1 Appendix English verbatim including its terminal periods. option_text carries anchors only where the source names them: the article states 'a Likert scale ranging from 1 = "strongly disagree" to 7 = "strongly agree"', so resp 1 and 7 are labelled and resp 2-6 are left blank rather than padded with their own numbers. Those anchors are the article's English gloss of French anchors it never prints, the same fallback as the item wording. instructions is blank - no instruction stem is published in either paper. correct_response blank (attitude scale, no key). section_id is the trivial single value with no section_prompt. (5) STEP 3b: instrument confirmed. Live data is 3 items on resp 1-7 with n=1010 per item, which equals the number of rows with complete Opt_1..Opt_3 in the deposit (674 at wave 0 plus 336 at wave 5); this matches the CPC-12 optimism subscale (3 items, 1-7) and not any other instrument in the battery. The sibling CPC-12 facets (hope Hope_1-3, self-efficacy SAE_1-3) are separate IRW tables and none of their columns appear here; the CPC-12's resilience facet was not administered.
